image_description: An underwater scene depicting a large school of hammerhead sharks swimming in blue water. The sharks are viewed from various angles, primarily side and top-down profiles. A scuba diver is visible in the mid-ground, providing scale. The foreground features a prominent hammerhead shark swimming right-to-left, while numerous others fade into the background haze. The lighting is diffuse, typical of underwater environments.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The primary subject in the foreground and several background subjects clearly display the characteristic T-shaped or hammer-shaped head structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: On the clearest foreground shark, dark spots consistent with eyes are visible at the outermost edges of the hammer structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution and water turbidity prevent clear visualization of nostrils on any individual shark.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge of the cephalofoil on the foreground shark appears straight/slightly curved, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fins visible on the foreground and mid-ground sharks are tall, triangular/falcate, and positioned correctly behind the pectoral fins.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fins visible on several sharks show the characteristic heterocercal shape with a larger upper lobe.

A cluster of sharks in the mid-right background appears to have fused fins or indistinct boundaries where bodies overlap, suggesting minor structural coherence issues in complex occlusion scenarios.
